title: Adaptive fairness stream harness: multi-tenant token pacing + p95/regression gates for SSE & WebSocket
creator: Anjali Rao
description: Build a next-generation load testing harness that can simulate multi-tenant streaming chat/completion workloads over SSE and WebSocket with adaptive priority and fairness controls. The harness should model realistic token emission rates, KV-cache warm/cold behavior, token-level pacing, and transient network conditions (jitter, packet loss, reconnects). It must produce telemetry suitable for p95 latency tracking, tokens/sec throughput, and automated regression detection against a historical baseline. This ticket covers design, an initial implementation for the most common protocols (SSE + WebSocket), telemetry hooks to Redwood Console dashboards, and a regression detector that can run nightly and produce alerts when token-level p95 or error-rate regress beyond configured thresholds.
acceptance_criteria: Simulator can run 10k concurrent streaming sessions across SSE and WebSocket split configurable by tenant mix
Per-tenant priority and fairness policy implemented: high/medium/low weight groups and token-budget enforcement
KV cache modeling: session types for warm (reused cache) and cold (miss-first N requests) with configurable percentiles
Collected metrics include tokens/sec (global and per-tenant), p50/p95/p99 generation latency per request, reconnect/error rates, and percent of requests served from cache
Nightly regression job compares latest p95 tokens/sec-normalized latency to 28-day rolling baseline and opens an alert ticket if >8% degradation sustained over 3 runs
End-to-end demo run outputs JSON summary compatible with existing benchmarking dashboard and links to generated traces
Documentation (README) with runbook, knobs, example configs, and sample tenant profiles
Safety: harness respects rate limits and can be run against staging only; config prevents accidental production blast radius
implementation_notes: Language: Go for core load driver (low-latency net IO) + Python companion for orchestration and regression analysis
Connection pooler per process with per-tenant multiplexing to model realistic browser vs mobile clients
Token pacing implemented as leaky-bucket at per-connection and per-tenant levels to reproduce backpressure behaviors
KV-cache simulator emits TTL and hit/miss events; integrate with runtime KV cache tags to mark warm/cold sessions
Telemetry: emit structured metrics to Prometheus + trace spans to OpenTelemetry (for console ingestion). Push summary JSON to S3 for nightly analysis
Regression detector: incremental model that stores per-config baselines in S3/BigTable and computes stat-significant changes (bootstrap CI on p95 samples)
CI: unit tests for pacing logic, property tests for fairness weights, integration test that runs a 100-session smoke harness in CI
telemetry: traces: span names: driver.connect, session.init, token.emit, session.close (with attributes)
test_plans: Baseline sweep: run 1k, 5k, 10k sessions with tenant mixes: [90% low, 10% high], [50/30/20], [25/25/25/25]
KV scenarios: 0% warm, 30% warm, 80% warm to measure cache impact on p95
Network fuzz: add jitter 10-200ms, intermittent 1% packet loss, simulated reconnect every 5-30 minutes
Fairness validation: ensure high-priority tenants maintain SLA when total capacity constrained by throttling to 60%
Regression test: run nightly pipeline that computes delta against 28-day rolling baseline and validates against thresholds (p95 and error-rate)
Blameless-runbook: include steps to abort runs, collect artifacts, and revert harness changes
